An opponent or enemy.

examples.text: [H]is eyes vacant—his face haggard—his head drooping, the spectacle of such an antagonist to the vigorous Edward, moved only pity in the few, and ridicule in the many.

glosses: One who antagonizes or stirs.
A chemical that binds to a receptor but does not produce a physiological response, blocking the action of other agonist chemicals, such as endogenous chemical messengers.

examples.text: 2001: The calcium antagonists represent one of the top ten classes of prescription drugs in terms of commercial value, with worldwide sales of nearly $10 billion in 1999. — Leslie Iversen, Drugs: A Very Short Introduction (Oxford 2001, p. 41)

glosses: The main character or force opposing the protagonist in a literary work or drama.

examples.text: So God forbid I'm seen just as an average human being / I mean, imagine if antagonists lacked any evil scheme

glosses: A muscle that acts in opposition to another.

examples.text: A flexor, which bends a part, is the antagonist of an extensor, which extends it.

glosses: Que se opone a algo, que lucha contra ello o antagoniza.
Se dice de un diente, hueso, músculo o cualquier otra parte anatómica estructuralmente opuesta a otra llamada agonista.
Se dice de la sustancia que tiene efectos contrarios o que bloquea a los agonistas.
Persona o cosa que está opuesta a otra o que es contraria a otra.
Personaje en una historia o en un obra literaria que lucha en contra del protagonista.
истор. в древнегреческой драме — персонаж, активно противодействующий основному герою (протагонисту) на пути к достижению его целей
перен., книжн. непримиримый противник
хим. вещество, биологическое действие которого противоположно действию другого вещества — агониста

examples.text: Комбинированный препарат, в составе которого симпатомиметик фенилэфрин и антагонист гистаминовых рецепторов диметинден.
